messages:
marta: Quick check — during the canary we pulled verbose debug logs from the batch worker. Any chance customer tokens ended up in stdout? Trying to scope exposure before we escalate.
alex: I ran a quick grep across the canary logs, no Bearer/api_key patterns found. Command I used: ```grep -E \"(Bearer|api_key|token)\" /var/log/canary/*.log || echo no matches``` — returned \"no matches\".
shay: I did notice one raw user_input line that included an email address, not a token. Example (sanitized): ```[INFO] user_input=\"Please reset my password for alice@example.com\"``` — appears to be PII, not auth secret.
marta: Good catch. So two buckets: secrets (tokens) vs PII (emails). If secrets were leaked -> customer comms + rotation. If only PII -> internal incident, redact logs and check backups. Can we confirm which it is?
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-42 — severity: low, tags: privacy-check, owner: eng-oncall
dara: Ran an audit query against the stored payloads: ```SELECT count(*) FROM logs WHERE env='canary' AND payload ILIKE '%Bearer%'``` -> 0. Also filtered for common api_key patterns -> 0. No production customer IDs matched; matches are test-account UUIDs.
ops: @security-team ping — please confirm whether this requires external comms or internal closure only.
alex: My recommendation: treat as PII-only. Action items: 1) redact the email from the canary logs in S3, 2) rotate any test creds found, 3) scan backups for matches. I'll open a PR to add a redaction lambda and queue the rotate job.
marta: Thanks. @emily can you sign off on internal-only? Once approved we'll run redaction and close. Also want a short note to execs describing impact (none on customers).
emily: Reviewed the results and queries. Confirmed no auth tokens or customer identifiers were exposed. OK to keep internal and mark as privacy-check closed. :white_check_mark:
dara: Ran redaction job, rotated test creds, scanned backups — no matches. Updated incident INC-2026-42 with remediation steps and artifacts.
marta: Great — thanks everyone. Closing thread after I add a one-paragraph summary for the postmortem doc.
